Hardcoded Radio `name="options"` Causes Global Collision Across Instances - **Evidence**: Line 13: ```jsx name="options" ``` - **Impacted User Group**: Keyboard-only users, screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users. - **Why this matters**: The HTML specification defines radio group mutual exclusion and arrow-key focus scoping by the `name` attribute within the document or form. Because `name="options"` is hardcoded, if two `BuggyRadioGroup` instances exist on the same page (e.g., *"Size"* and *"Color"*): 1. Arrow-key navigation in the first group navigates straight into the second group. 2. Selecting an option in the second group unselects the user's choice in the first group in the DOM. 3. Screen reader position announcements report inaccurate group counts (e.g., *"1 of 6"* instead of *"1 of 3"*). - **Standards Grounding**: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard - Level A), SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order - Level A), SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value - Level A). - **Fix**: Accept a `name` prop or generate an instance-unique fallback using React 18's `useId()` hook: `const generatedName = useId(); const groupName = name || generatedName;`. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: radio-hardcoded-name-collision fingerprint: a81d94f2bc4389e1 source: BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:13 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1 Keyboard, SC 2.4.3 Focus Order, SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value section_508_fpc_context: WCAG 2.0 SC 2.1.1 / 4.1.2 (mapped to Section 508 501.1 / 504.2) severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: keyboard=MEDIUM, screen_reader=HIGH, cognitive=MEDIUM evidence: BuggyRadioGroup.jsx:13: name="options" reproduction_steps: 1.
